pairs.subject: credential-vault
pairs.evidence: crates/table-runtime/src/configuration.rs:245 Channel3 credentials enter persistent custody after syntax checks without live validation, allowing an unusable key to be admitted.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-runtime/src/configuration.rs:238 Admission checks string shape, then stores the key without an authenticated validation or baseline identity and scopes.
crates/table-runtime/src/market.rs:41 The vault adapter returns the actual credential to the market client, which attaches it to requests; the standard requires actions to cross the custody boundary.

crates/table-market/src/lib.rs:101 Authenticated calls collapse authentication rejection and provider failures into the same unavailable result; no separate credential probe or timestamped verdict is implemented.
crates/table-runtime/src/configuration.rs:239 This context retains a static API key, without an issuer lease, renewal increment or renewable duration.
crates/table-market/src/lib.rs:41 The cache holds market references, not leased credentials served to consumers.
crates/table-runtime/src/configuration.rs:516 Replacement overwrites the incumbent credential directly, without validating the successor or retaining the incumbent until successful successor traffic.
crates/table-market/src/lib.rs:71 Requests use the stored API key directly; this context has no grant-to-access-token exchange or refresh-token lifecycle.
crates/table-runtime/src/market.rs:37 The market adapter reads a foreign provider credential; it does not mint or manage a family of sealing-key versions.
